merge_method.problem: The r9 repair lineages are disjoint and each is a strict subset of the union. S17 patched the INSTALLED tools. S18 wrote a separate guard + three suffixed candidates that are pre-S17 bodies plus late-loaded overrides. Appending the guard to S17 does not compose them: the guard redefines same-named helpers, silently dropping S17 fixes; adopting the S18 candidates wholesale drops the S17 fixes the same way.

measured_proof_of_both_loss_directions.installed_S17_tools_on_merged_harness: verify 18/7, vault 19/6, quarantine 32/6 — the failures are the S18 families (dirty-pushed, hidden live refs, ignored directory payload, self-referential ledger row, unpushed-stale fallback, symlinked quarantine root) plus the two S15-adopted classes
measured_proof_of_both_loss_directions.S18_candidates_on_merged_harness: verify 21/4, vault 21/4, quarantine 21/17 — the failures are the S17 families (ledger revocation after capture on file and directory paths; NUL list gate; default-ref rollback and missing default ref in the second check) plus the two S15-adopted classes. Caveat: the harness exports SOUJI_VERIFY_BIN, so the r9-s18 quarantine candidate is measured against the INSTALLED engine rather than its own sibling, which inflates its failure count; the verify/vault figures are unaffected.
measured_proof_of_both_loss_directions.conclusion: neither lineage alone is sufficient; the composed tool is base union guard, not a copy of either

merge_method.composition: base = S17 body; guard = S18 shared hardening inlined after the base's function definitions so it overrides same-named helpers; renames = the minimum needed so the guard's delegating wrappers resolve to the S17 implementation instead of recursing; union patches = the two places where an override would otherwise DROP an S17 fix

renames.verify: evaluate_path -> s18_evaluate_path (guard wrapper delegates to it)
renames.vault: evaluate_path -> s18_evaluate_path; try_ledger -> s18_try_ledger (the guard's strict row filter delegates to it, so row validation AND the revocation pin both run)
renames.quarantine: flow_one -> s18_flow_one; second_check -> s18_second_check (guard containment wrappers delegate to them)

union_patches.verify.try_obsidian: guard override would drop the S17 ledger-revocation pin; the composed version keeps the guard's strict independent-row validation AND compares the ledger digest before returning SAFE
union_patches.vault.load_ledger: guard override would drop LEDGER_PIN capture; the composed version keeps the guard's path validation AND captures the pin
union_patches.quarantine.VERIFY_BIN: the composed quarantine defaults to its merged sibling engine when present, else the installed engine, so the pair is exercised as a unit

adopted_cross_cluster_fixes.finding: `git diff --quiet <ref> -- <path>` rewrites .git/index on git 2.55 to refresh stat info. GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0 does NOT suppress it for this subcommand (measured in isolation, four variants: plain, env GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0, --no-optional-locks, --exit-code — all four WRITE). S13's cluster-G1 case flags the installed tools too, so this is inherited, not merge-induced.
adopted_cross_cluster_fixes.fix: s18_snapshot_equal: a private index (read-tree + update-index -q --refresh + diff-index --quiet) reproduces the same tracked-content-vs-ref semantics and touches nothing in the repository

adopted_cross_cluster_fixes.source: S13/S14 cluster G (independently authored ctime witness in both)
adopted_cross_cluster_fixes.finding: an aged .scratch container whose descendant was rewritten and backdated earned SAFE(stale) and the live subtree was DELETED
adopted_cross_cluster_fixes.fix: s18_old_scope now requires every DESCENDANT to be old by mtime AND ctime; ctime is the one witness utime cannot forge backward. Root mtime semantics are unchanged.
adopted_cross_cluster_fixes.disclosed_trade_off: S08's cluster-D control case T ages its fixture with utime, which is exactly the forgery shape this rule refuses. A naturally aged artifact has an old ctime and still qualifies (verified on this host: utime moved mtime 6 days back and left ctime at now). This is a fixture-vs-rule collision, reported, not hidden.
